thread.title: Apple: We Might Be Inching Closer to ‘Apple Prime’

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Apple: We Might Be Inching Closer to ‘Apple Prime’
text:
Photo: Bloomberg News By David Marino-Nachison June 28, 2018 1:54 p.m. ET We seem to be getting closer to “Apple Prime .”
Or the “ Apple Bundle.”
Or the “Apple Extra Value Meal.” Or — whatever you want to call the as-yet-unannounced offering into which Apple (AAPL) would combine a suite of services for a single price.
Newsletter Sign-up On Thursday, The Information, citing “people familiar with the company’s plans,” reported that Apple planned to combine news, magazine articles and television into a single subscription product. Earlier this month, The Wall Street Journal reported that such a service might include iCloud storage as well . Apple bought a digital magazine service in March; some have speculated about other possibilities, such as health monitoring.
The company did not immediately respond to a Thursday afternoon email with requests for confirmation and follow-up questions. (We’ll add anything notable that we receive.) But the reports do fit the broader narrative around the Barron’s Next 50 tech giant, which is evolving into a company for which recurring service revenue is increasingly important even as it continues to tweak and add product lines in search of continued growth.
“We forecast Apple’s revenue surpassing >$260B in CY18E (+9%Y/Y), meaning that to keep growing even 5% from there it would need to keep adding the equivalent of a Fortune 200 company each year,” Guggenheim analysts noted Thursday. Not all analysts are convinced that Apple services are the best way forward in the long term, however.
Would you buy the Apple, er, value meal? You might, especially if you’re already a customer of one or more of the company’s other subscription services. Given sufficient consumer perception of value, that could considerably lower the chance a customer unsubscribes. (Though it’s certainly possible, or even likely, that Apple services would also be sold a la carte.)
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 An obvious comparison is Amazon.com (AMZN) Prime, though its services match Apple’s hypothetical offering in some categories and are completely different in many others; you probably shouldn’t expect clothing delivery , for example.
What’s certain is that consumers aren’t likely to hear the end of offers to give them various things in exchange for a neat little monthly fee anytime soon. Many of those offerings can surely coexist in the same household.
